'''Ame-no-Ikutama-no-Mikoto''' (天活玉命) is a [[Deity|kami]] appearing in [[Japanese mythology]].
In the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], this deity is referred to as '''Ikutama no Kami''' (生霊神), while the [[Kujiki|Sendai Kuji Hongi]] uses the name '''Ikutama no Mikoto''' (活玉命). He is venerated as an important deity in the [[Hasshinden]]. The [[Kojiki-den|Kojikiden]] identifies him with the deity [[Tsunugui and Ikugui|Tsunugui and Ikugui]].
According to the [[Kujiki|Sendai Kuji Hongi]], Amatsu Ikutama no Mikoto was one of the 32 deities who accompanied [[Nigihayahi no Mikoto|Nigihayahi]], and he is considered an ancestor of the Nittabe clan. The [[Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Shōjiroku]] identifies him as an ancestor of the [[Onchi Kannushi]].<ref>「河内国 神別 天神 恩智神主」『新撰姓氏録』、弘仁六年。</ref>
In the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], during the [[Jinshin War|Jinshin War]], it is said that the High Chief of Takichi, [[Takichi Kouno|Takechi no Kome]], suddenly lost his ability to speak. After three days, he was possessed by a deity who proclaimed, "I am the deity residing at the Takichi Shrine, [[Kotoshironushi|Kotoshironushi]], and also the deity residing at the [[Ikukunitama Shrine|Ikukunitama Shrine]]." The deity instructed the offering of horses and various weapons to the mausoleum of Emperor [[Emperor Jimmu|Jimmu]] and claimed to have accompanied Emperor [[Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] to protect him during his journey.
== Overview ==
In the '''Nihon Shoki''' (『日本書紀』), he is known as '''Seirei-shin''' (生霊神), and in the '''Sendaikyuji Honki''' (『先代旧事本紀』), he is known by the alias '''Akitama-no-Mikoto''' (活玉命). He is also worshipped as an important deity in [[Hachigoden|Hasshinden]]. In '''Kojiki Den''' (『古事記伝』), there is a theory that equates him with [[Tsunugui and Ikugui|Katsuragami]].
In the '''Sendaikyuji Honki''' (『先代旧事本紀』), he is regarded as one of the thirty-two gods who accompanied [[Narahasuhiko-no-Mikoto|Narahasuhiko-no-Mikoto]], and is considered the ancestor of [[Onchi Jiminushi|Onchi Jiminushi]] and the [[Nittambe Clan|Nittambe Clan]]. In '''Shinsen Sei Shiryo Roku''' (『新撰姓氏録』), he is described as the ancestor of [[Onchi Jiminushi|Onchi Jiminushi]].<ref>「河内国　神別　天神　恩智神主」『新撰姓氏録』、弘仁六年。</ref>
According to the '''Nihon Shoki''' (『日本書紀』), during the [[Jinshin War|壬申の乱1=Jinshin War]], [[Takai Kogume-no-Mikoto|Takai Kogume-no-Mikoto]], the lord of [[:en:Takaichi District, Nara|Takai-gun}}, suddenly lost his speech and became unable to speak. Three days later, a god appeared to Kogume and said:
"I am the [[Kotoshironushi|Jidai-no-kami]] at [[Takai-sha|Takai-sha]]. I am also the [[Seirei-shin|Seirei-shin]] at [[Misasa-sha|Misasa-sha]]."
"I offer horses and various weapons at the mausoleum of [[Emperor Jimmu|Jimmu Tennō]]."
"I stood before and after [[Tenmu Tennō|Emperor Tenmu]]'s grandson, and after sending to [[Fuwa District, Gifu|Fuwa-gun]], I have returned. Now I am appearing within the imperial army to protect it."
"Armies are approaching from the west. Be vigilant."
He is said to be the descendant of [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]'s child [[Tenninugohine-no-Mikoto|Tenninugohine-no-Mikoto]] according to '''Kojiki''' (『古事記』) and '''Shinsen Sei Shiryo Roku''' (『新撰姓氏録』).
